about: #4628: each surviving det-port mutant stated `equivalent` or `unreachable`, with the Java change and why it cannot alter observable behaviour; proposed in a PR, reviewed by the owner. A run that kills a stated mutant fails (the claim was wrong). Ids are mutation.py's; before / after are the Java line.

verdicts.equivalent: the change cannot alter anything the program shows (output, screen, files, COMMAREA, abend)
verdicts.unreachable: no input of the program reaches the changed code
verdicts.undefined-by-ibm: only non-digit data in a numeric USAGE DISPLAY item kills it, and IBM documents no result for that
verdicts.harness-gap: the change alters behaviour the proof runs but does not compare (open: the harness must)
verdicts.case-gap: an input the case lacks would kill it (open: strengthen the case)

image byte 0 of s_WS_BLOG is BLOG-TAG(1): both arms of the IF MOVE 'B1 ' or 'B2 ' over all 3 tag bytes before LOG-B, the only reader (WRITEQ TS FROM(WS-BLOG)); initialState() restores the image on every entry, so the first byte never reaches the queue. Ten new inputs left it alive.
every read of image byte(s) [0] of s_DFHEIBLK follows a top-level Cobol.store in its own method (inert-image)

byte 0 of the 2-byte GG_RETURN_CODE image becomes X'5C': the item is read only by the returnCode() accessor after the run, which no compared scenario reads (the harness compares screen, COMMAREA, TS writes and abend), and PCIMMB never stores RETURN-CODE. Ten new inputs left it alive. Open: the harness does not compare the return code.
f2_WS_BLOG is read only by DetCics.padded(f2_WS_BLOG, 15, ...), which copies min(15, f.length()) bytes: length 16 copies the same 15. Ten new inputs left it alive.
